steps.title: going to
steps.html:
FormExample
Positiveam / is / are + going to + verbShe's going to move house.
Negativeam not / isn't / aren't + going toWe're not going to join a gym.
QuestionAm / Is / Are + person + going toAre you going to visit him?
Wh- questionWh- + am / is / are + going toWhat are you going to do?
Short answerYes, I am. / No, I'm not.

The first part is to be, exactly as in the Present Continuous from Lesson 18.

After going to the verb is the base form: going to move, not going to moves.

Use it for a decision you have already made. It is not a guess about the weather.

Learners often drop the first part. I going to travel needs am.

steps.title: Listen. The word to almost disappears.
steps.sub: But in a negative sentence, not is strong.

items.text: In going to we do not stress to — and in negatives we stress not.
